Native first- or second-order functional trajectory differentiation

etr_differentiate_trajectories.Rd

Pure R numerical analogue of frozen eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0 differentiate_trajectories. Uses the source-compatible second-order edge-aware gradient on the recorded, potentially nonuniform time grid; no smoothing, time-grid resampling or Python execution is involved.

Usage

etr_differentiate_trajectories(x, order = 1L)

Arguments

x

Complete native etr_trajectory_set with at least three distinct time samples.

order

Derivative order 1 or 2. Python-like Boolean TRUE is accepted as order 1; FALSE, non-integral values, missing and out-of-range orders are rejected.

Value

An etr_trajectory_set with one derivative channel per original channel; suffixes _velocity (order 1) and _acceleration (order 2). Original curve IDs, time, metadata, coordinate system, time unit and nonoverwritten provenance keys are preserved. The source provenance$derivative mapping records the order, numpy_gradient numerical method and smoothing=FALSE.

Details

For order 2 the second derivative is obtained by differentiating the first derivative again using an irregular-grid second-order edge-aware stencil. There is no hidden smoothing and no measurement uncertainty correction. This source-aligned method is distinct from the historical R convenience methods etr_velocity and etr_acceleration, whose default output/provenance contracts are left unchanged.

Tests against pinned Python 1.2 are first-party qualification evidence only; full input-domain parity, all source representations and independent scientific certification remain open.

Examples

t <- c(0, 0.2, 0.7, 1.5)
v <- array(t^2, dim = c(1L, length(t), 1L))
x <- etr_trajectory_set(t, v, dimension_names = "x")
first <- etr_differentiate_trajectories(x, order = 1L)
second <- etr_differentiate_trajectories(x, order = 2L)
